source_text: Si uetera fidei exempla, et Dei gratiam testificantia et aedificationem hominis operantia, propterea in litteris sunt digesta, ut lectione eorum quasi repraesentatione rerum et deus honoretur et homo confortetur: cur non et noua documenta aeque utrique causae conuenientia et digerantur? Uel quia proinde et haec uetera futura quandoque sunt et necessaria posteris, si in praesenti suo tempore minori deputantur auctoritati, propter praesumptam uenerationem antiquitatis. Sed uiderint qui unam uirtutem spiritus unius sancti pro aetatibus iudicent temporum: cum maiora reputanda sunt nouitiora quaeque ut nouissimiora, secundum exuperationem gratiae in ultima saeculi spatia decretam. In nouissimis enim diebus, dicit dominus, effundam de spiritu meo super omnem carnem, et prophetabunt filii filiaeque eorum; et super seruos et ancillas meas de meo spiritu effundam: et iuuenes uisiones uidebunt, et senes somnia somniabunt. Itaque et nos, qui sicut prophetias ita et uisiones nouas pariter repromissas et agnoscimus et honoramus, ceterasque uirtutes spiritus sancti ad instrumentum ecclesiae deputatas (cui et missus est idem omnia donatiua administrans in omnibus prout uni cuique distribuit dominus) necessario et digerimus et ad gloriam dei lectione celebramus, ut ne qua aut imbecillitas aut desperatio fidei apud ueteres tantum aestimet gratiam diuinitus conuersatam, siue in martyrum siue in reuelationum dignatione: cum semper deus operetur quae repromisit, non credentibus in testimonium, credentibus in beneficium. Sed nos itaque quod audiuimus et contrectauimus annuntiamus et uobis, fratres et filioli: ut et uos qui interfuistis rememoremini gloriae domini, et qui nunc cognoscitis per auditum communionem habeatis cum sanctis martyribus, et per illos cum domino Iesu Christo: cui est claritas et honor in saecula saeculorum, amen.
pass_a_gloss: Literal gloss: if old faith-examples, witnessing God's grace and producing man's building-up, were written down for this reason — so that by their reading, as a re-presentation of deeds, God be honored and man be strengthened — why should new evidences, equally fitting for each purpose, not also be written down? Or also because these new things will themselves one day be old and needed by descendants, if in their own present time they are counted of lesser authority because of assumed reverence for antiquity. Let those answer who judge one power of one Holy Spirit by ages of times, whereas newer/latest things are to be counted greater, according to the overflow of grace decreed for the final stretches of the age. For the Lord says in the last days he will pour from his Spirit on all flesh, sons and daughters will prophesy, on his menservants and maidservants he will pour from his Spirit, youths will see visions and old men will dream dreams. Therefore we who acknowledge and honor both prophecies and new visions alike as promised, and the other powers of the Holy Spirit as assigned to the equipment of the Church — to whom the same Spirit was sent, administering all gifts among all as the Lord apportions to each — both write them down of necessity and celebrate them by reading to God's glory, lest any weakness or despair of faith suppose divine grace conversed only among ancients, whether in conferral of martyrdoms or of revelations, since God always effects what he promised, to unbelievers for testimony, to believers for benefit. So what we heard and touched we announce also to you, brothers and little children, so that both you who were present may recall the Lord's glory, and you who now learn by hearing may have communion with the holy martyrs, and through them with the Lord Jesus Christ, to whom is brightness and honor unto ages of ages, amen.
pass_b_english: If the old examples of faith, which testify to the grace of God and build up man, were for this reason committed to writing, so that by the reading of them, as a making-present of the deeds, God might be honored and man might be strengthened, why should not new testimonies also, equally suited to each end, be committed to writing? Or for this reason too, that these present things will themselves one day be old and necessary for those to come, even if in their own present time they are reckoned of lesser authority because of the reverence presumed due to antiquity. Let those answer who judge the one power of the one Holy Spirit by the ages of the seasons, whereas the newer things, as the latest, are to be reckoned the greater, according to the surpassing abundance of grace decreed for the last reaches of the age. For in the last days, says the Lord, I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh, and their sons and their daughters shall prophesy; and upon my servants and my handmaids I will pour out from my Spirit, and the young men shall see visions, and the old men shall dream dreams (Joel 2:28-29; Acts 2:17-18). Therefore we also, who acknowledge and honor both prophecies and new visions alike as things promised, and reckon the other powers of the Holy Spirit as appointed for the furnishing of the Church, to whom the same Spirit was also sent, administering all his gifts among all as the Lord apportions to each one, both of necessity commit them to writing and celebrate them by reading to the glory of God, lest any weakness or despair of faith should suppose that grace from God conversed only among those of old, whether in the bestowal of martyrdoms or of revelations, since God always works what he has promised, to those who do not believe for a testimony, to those who believe for a benefit. And so what we have heard and handled we announce also to you, brethren and little children (1 John 1:1,3), so that both you who were present may remember the glory of the Lord, and you who now learn by hearing may have fellowship with the holy martyrs, and through them with the Lord Jesus Christ, to whom is brightness and honor unto ages of ages, amen.

choices.why: neuter plural in parallel with exempla; context is recent martyrdoms and visions to be written and read, so evidential records rather than doctrine
singular virtus with genitive denotes operative power, contrasted with division by ages; not moral virtue here
instrumentum with dative/genitive sense of equipment for use; deputatas shows appointment to service, not a written instrument
